name: Salerno
title: Salerno Ship Gauging: UTM for Container, Ro-Ro & Car Carriers
description: Thickness measurement at Salerno for container ships, ro-ro and car carriers and ferries: hull, deck and ramp gauging for survey and pre-docking use.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging for Ships at the Port of Salerno
intro: Salerno handles containers, trailers and vehicles at a scale that makes it one of southern Italy's busiest commercial ports, with ro-ro and ferry lines running to Sicily, Malta, North Africa and Spain. A ship worked here is usually on a fixed weekly rotation, so Atlantis NDT sends a team from India to take thickness readings during the cargo stop, concentrating on decks, ramps, ballast tanks and hull areas due for survey.

highlights.h: Weekly ro-ro rotations give repeat access
highlights.p: Ro-ro and car carrier services call at Salerno on a regular schedule. A ship that returns every few days offers repeated windows to gauge ramps, car decks and tanks as part of a longer programme.

highlights.h: Container and trailer trades in one port
highlights.p: Container ships, trailer carriers and vehicle carriers share the harbour, so one visit can cover very different structures, from container hatch cover areas to hoistable car decks.
Passenger vessels serving the coast and islands add small passenger craft to the port's traffic. They are inspected in the off-season, when lay-up gives more time than the busy summer timetable.

port.h: The port of Salerno: containers, vehicles and Mediterranean ro-ro links
p: Salerno lies at the head of the Gulf of Salerno, south of Naples, and shares its port authority with Naples and Castellammare di Stabia. The harbour is sheltered by breakwaters and entered from the open Tyrrhenian, with no tidal gate and no lock, so a ship can come alongside as soon as pilots and tugs are in place. The port occupies a long strip of waterfront, with container operations at one end, ro-ro and trailer berths in the middle and passenger quays close to the old town, and the layout makes it practical to reach several ships in a single day.

Containers and rolling cargo are what Salerno is known for. Container ships bring feeder and short-sea boxes to a terminal that serves the industry of Campania and the south, and ro-ro lines connect the port with Sicily, Malta, Tunisia and the Spanish ports on regular schedules, carrying trailers, vehicles and project cargo. Car carriers and ro-ro ships unload new and used vehicles here for distribution inland. These ships operate to the clock, and a delay at the berth is expensive to the operator, so any inspection has to be prepared well enough to use the time without slowing cargo work.

The passenger business is smaller but visible. Cruise calls use the passenger quay, and ferries and fast craft run along the Amalfi Coast and to the islands in season, with timetables tightening from spring to autumn. For thickness gauging the contrast between the trades is useful: commercial ships in steady rotation allow repeated short visits throughout the year, while passenger craft are best looked at in the quieter months. Salerno ships often dock at larger yards in Naples or Palermo, which makes Salerno a convenient place to take pre-docking readings before the ship moves.

facilities.h: Where thickness gauging can be carried out at Salerno
p: Salerno is a commercial port, so gauging is mostly done alongside. Each ship's call is short, and the programme has to fit between discharge and loading, between passenger disembarkation and boarding, or inside a planned lay-up period. In practice that means choosing a handful of accessible spaces per visit: a ramp and its supporting structure, a car deck section, a few ballast tanks the crew can ventilate, or the hatch coamings on a container ship. Where the owner wants more, the work is spread across several calls and compiled into a single set of results.

Ships that need a full docking survey typically leave Salerno for a yard with the right drydock, and Naples, only a short voyage away, is the most common destination, followed by Palermo. Pre-docking readings at Salerno give the superintendent a working steel estimate to put into the yard specification before the ship sails. Some passenger craft and workboats are hauled out at smaller yards on the coast, and where an owner has ships at both Salerno and neighbouring ports, a single mobilisation by road can cover them.
list: Container terminal berths — hatch coaming, cell guide and ballast tank gauging on feeder and short-sea container ships during the cargo stop
Ro-ro and trailer berths — ramp, stern door and car deck structure gauged on ships that return to Salerno on weekly schedules
Vehicle carrier berths — hoistable deck, side shell and tank readings on car carriers after discharge
Passenger quay and ferry berths — cruise ships and coastal ferries gauged during turnaround, or in lay-up outside the summer season
Roads in the gulf — owner's condition and pre-purchase gauging on ships at anchor, using a launch arranged through the agent
Naples and Castellammare di Stabia — neighbouring ports and repair yards, often joined to a Salerno visit in the same mobilisation

context.h: Port state control, rolling-cargo rules and the Campania trades
p: Salerno follows the Paris MoU port state control system used across Italy, with inspections carried out by the Guardia Costiera. Ro-ro cargo ships and car carriers often show structural damage in the places that matter to inspectors: ramps, internal decks and lashing points are worn by constant vehicle movement, and watertight doors and hoistable decks need to be sound. Ferries and passenger craft in scheduled service are covered by the EU's additional inspection regime, which applies to the Amalfi Coast and island services as well as to the long-haul lines.

European rules shape the decisions owners make here. The Ship Recycling Regulation asks for an Inventory of Hazardous Materials on ships calling at EU ports, and many owners complete it alongside a major survey. EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime affect the bigger ro-ro and container ships calling at Salerno, which pushes owners of older vessels to assess the remaining life of their steel against alternatives. Measured thickness records, taken during short stops in a busy commercial port, are a practical basis for that assessment.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Salerno
jobs.p: Work at Salerno is built around short, repeatable visits. A ro-ro ship on a weekly rotation might be looked at in three or four stages across a month, a container feeder in a single cargo stop, and a passenger craft during winter lay-up. We prepare a measurement plan for each ship, stick to the spaces that can be opened safely in the time available, and consolidate everything into one report so that the surveyor or yard has a single record.
list: Ramp, stern door and car deck readings on a ro-ro ship at Salerno, repeated across several weekly calls ahead of a renewal survey
Hatch coaming and ballast tank gauging on a feeder container ship during its cargo stop at the container terminal
Hoistable deck and side shell measurement on a car carrier after discharge, supporting a steel estimate for docking in Naples
Winter lay-up gauging on a coastal ferry or fast craft, with time to open tanks and measure the hull thoroughly
Pre-purchase condition gauging on a second-hand ro-ro or container ship at anchor in the Gulf of Salerno

logistics: Naples International Airport is the nearest main gateway and Salerno is reached from it by road or by rail, while Rome Fiumicino adds long-haul options. The ship's agent arranges ISPS passes for the commercial and passenger berths and a launch for ships at anchor. The inspection team travels from India and needs Schengen visas, so owners should confirm dates with enough lead time; ro-ro schedules repeat predictably, which usually makes that easier than for one-off calls.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a ro-ro ship at Salerno without delaying cargo work?
faqs.a: Yes, if the programme is planned around the loading and discharge sequence. We start with spaces away from the working ramp, such as ballast tanks and upper decks, and come to ramps and car decks when they are clear. Agents and the master confirm the timing before the ship arrives.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Salerno for survey dockings?
faqs.a: Salerno is a commercial and passenger port rather than a major repair centre. Ships usually dock at Naples, which is close, or at a yard elsewhere in the Mediterranean. We take pre-docking readings at Salerno so the owner can set a realistic steel renewal plan before the ship leaves.

faqs.q: What gauging suits a feeder container ship during a Salerno call?
faqs.a: Hatch coamings and covers, selected ballast tanks, and any hull areas the surveyor has noted. Cargo stops are short, so we agree the list with the superintendent in advance and take the readings once the area is safe, then pass on a clear record the same day.

faqs.q: Can several ships be covered in one visit to the Gulf of Salerno?
faqs.a: Often. Container, ro-ro and passenger berths are within the same port, and Naples and Castellammare di Stabia are close by road. If you have more than one ship due in the same week, give us each schedule and we will plan the route so that the team's time is used across all of them.
